column1: # SSH public keys malware adds to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, a login to the computer for the attacker.
# One line each, tab separated. After editing, run: bash tools/gen.sh
#   incident  an id from data/incidents.tsv whose packages are only editor extensions
#             (data/bad-extensions.tsv): the key is shown with them, as that incident's sign
#   type      the key's type, as the line writes it before the key (ssh-ed25519, ssh-rsa, ecdsa-sha2-nistp256)
#   key       the key itself, its base64 text. A line of ~/.ssh/authorized_keys counts when the type and
#             then the key are two of its fields, whatever options come before them or comment after
#   note      what the key is, shown under ~/.ssh/authorized_keys
# These are public keys, published by the sources as signs of the incident, never secrets.
# Trojanized Claude Code extension (claudeext): StepSecurity's post gives the key, with the comment
# svc-telemetry; Cursor's security notice and StepSecurity give its fingerprint,
# SHA256:0Z6R+DF64Do2nwQic8a7kkfDLNNk4IiK+2U2Rci4htk, which ssh-keygen -lf gives for this line.

column4: the SSH key the trojanized Claude Code extension adds for the attacker
